summary: Ephemeral org-level read-only bridge for security permission scans across AWS/GCP
description:
Issue summary:
Security wants a short-lived, organization-scoped read-only access path (AWS assume-role + GCP workload identity) so the permission-scanner job can enumerate IAM roles, bindings, and service accounts across multiple accounts/projects for a quarterly audit. Current gaps: our scanner fails with AccessDenied on a subset of accounts and projects because there isn't a consistently provisioned org-level reader role or the trust relationship is missing.

Impact:
- Blocking scheduled security permission scans for prod and staging (quarterly audit).
- Delays ability to produce audit evidence for SOC2 readiness.
- Manual ad-hoc access requests are being used, creating an operational burden on SREs.

Request / Acceptance criteria:
- Create an ephemeral access flow that allows a Security-run job to obtain read-only credentials across targeted AWS accounts and GCP projects for up to 4 hours.
- Permissions must be strictly read-only: enumerate roles, list bindings, read policy documents, list service accounts, but NOT get service account keys or modify policies.
- Enforce JIT (just-in-time) issuance via an automated broker (Terraform + Lambda/Cloud Function) and audit logs for issuance/assumption events.
- IP allowlist for issuance (security team's egress ranges) and session tags that identify the runbook/job id.
- Provide runbook and automation PR that can be reviewed and promoted to prod.

Steps to reproduce (scanner failure example):
1) Run permission-scanner v2 against org-account: redwood-prod-ops (scanner invoked by security CI job).
2) Scanner errors out with: "AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/SecurityScanner is not authorized to perform: iam:ListRoles on resource: *" for accounts A/B/C.
3) In GCP, the scanner sees: "Permission denied: resourcemanager.organizations.get" when listing projects in org for some service accounts.

Initial notes and diagnostics:
- aws CloudTrail checks for last 90 days show repeated AssumeRole failures (see logs linked in comments).
- GCP audit logs show policy binding omissions for the service account used by the scanner in some folders.
- Existing ad-hoc approach used by SecOps: manual cross-account role creation with broad trust -> unacceptable for long term.

Proposed minimal operator change (temporary until infra automation lands):
- Provision a new role in each AWS account named RedwoodOrgAuditReader with attached AWS managed policy SecurityAudit plus a narrow inline policy to allow listing roles, policies, and service accounts but deny sensitive key operations. Configure trust policy to allow assumption from a single broker role in the central security account and require ExternalId matching the job run id.
- In GCP, create an organization-level group redwood-org-audit@redwood.com and grant roles/resourcemanager.organizationViewer + roles/iam.securityReviewer at org-level, but scope exceptions so that no service account key retrieval is allowed. Create a workload identity pool mapping to the security broker service account.
- TTL enforced via STS/session duration (AWS) and token TTL on the workload identity provider (GCP).

Documentation / runbook expectations:
- Short runbook for requesting a JIT token, how to run the scanner using the token, and how to revoke a token in an emergency.
- Sample CLI snippets and CI config that uses the broker endpoint.
investigation_notes:
2026-03-01: Ran permission-scanner v2 locally against 5 accounts; consistent failures on accounts that lacked an org-wide read role. CLI excerpts: 
- AWS error: "An error occurred (AccessDenied) when calling the ListRoles operation: User is not authorized to perform iam:ListRoles"
- GCP error: "Permission 'resourcemanager.organizations.get' denied on resource \"organizations/987654321\""

Checked account-role footprint: some accounts had a pre-existing role named 'OrgAudit' but no centralized trust to the security broker (missing sts:ExternalId or incorrect Principal).

Hypothesis: inconsistently provisioned roles + missing trust policies cause scanner to fall back to manual access paths.

Tests performed:
- Created a demo role with SecurityAudit in a non-prod account and allowed assumption from broker -> scanner succeeded when assuming role.
- Created workload identity binding in a test GCP project to the broker service account -> scanner succeeded for that project.

Risk assessment: low for read-only exposure if ExternalId + session tagging enforced and issuance audited. Need to ensure no admin-level permissions slip into custom policy.

resolution:
Provisioned a consistent org-scoped read-only access path for Security's permission scanner. Actions taken:
- AWS: Deployed 'redwood-org-audit' role in target accounts with SecurityAudit managed policy + narrow inline allow-list and explicit deny for key creation. Trust policy locked to security-broker role with ExternalId enforcement and session duration 4h.
- GCP: Created org group redwood-org-audit@redwood.com and granted read-only viewer + iam.securityReviewer roles where needed. Provisioned workload identity pool mapping the security broker SA to allow short-lived tokens.
- Automation: Merged infra PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1589) that creates roles/workload identity bindings from inventory.
- Runbook: Added a short JIT issuance runbook and emergency token revocation steps to Confluence.
Post-mortem / follow-up items:
1) Promote PR to remaining accounts with canary rollout and a 48h monitoring window.
2) Implement continuous attestation job to detect trust-policy drift.
3) Expand allowlist only after security review if additional scanner endpoints are required.
Ticket resolved after successful full-run verification on 2026-03-05.
next_steps: 1) Promote infra PR to prod across the remaining accounts during maintenance window (owners notified). 2) Implement the attestation check referenced in the resolution and add an alert to #security if the org role disappears or trust relationship changes. 3) Document the JIT broker SRE runbook and hand over to SecOps for quarterly runs.
notes: This ticket intentionally kept operator-facing detail (CLI snippets, CloudTrail links, PR) to help oncall runbook authors build the JIT flow. Keep secrets out of ticket comments; use secure storage for ExternalId secrets and broker credentials.
